title: Lemosho Route · 7 days
content:
Embark on a remarkable adventure climbing Kilimanjaro via the Lemosho Route. Your journey begins with a warm welcome at Kilimanjaro International Airport, followed by a smooth transfer to your Hotel. Here, you’ll receive a detailed briefing from our experienced guides, setting the stage for your trek. Enjoy the hotel’s amenities, including a pool, garden, bar, and restaurant, ensuring a comfortable start to your journey.

The trek kicks off with a drive to Lemosho Park Gate, where you’ll register before hiking through lush forest trails to Mti Mkubwa Camp. Over the following days, you’ll ascend through stunning landscapes, including Shira 1 and Shira 2 camps, the Lava Tower, and the famous Barranco Wall. Each day offers new challenges and breathtaking views, culminating in the summit attempt to Uhuru Peak.

After reaching the peak, you’ll descend to Mweka Camp and return to your Hotel for a hot meal and a chance to reflect on your achievement. Optional extensions include safaris and visits to Zanzibar, allowing further exploration of Tanzania’s diverse beauty.

This journey combines adventure with the opportunity to experience the breathtaking landscapes and rich culture of Tanzania, ensuring a memorable trip for every climber

faqs.title: How long does it take to climb Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: The duration of a Kilimanjaro climb typically ranges from 5 to 10 days, depending on the chosen route and your acclimatization needs. Longer treks allow for better acclimatization and increase the chances of reaching the summit.

faqs.title: What is the best time to climb Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: The best times to climb are during the dry seasons, which run from late June to October and from mid-January to March. These months generally offer clearer skies and better weather conditions.

faqs.title: Do I need to be an experienced climber to summit Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: No previous climbing experience is necessary to summit Kilimanjaro. However, a good level of physical fitness, preparation, and understanding of altitude sickness are important for a successful climb.

faqs.title: What are the different routes to climb Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: There are several routes to summit Kilimanjaro, including the Marangu, Machame, Lemosho, and Rongai routes. Each varies in difficulty, scenery, and duration, so choose one that aligns with your preferences and fitness level.

faqs.title: What should I pack for climbing Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: Essential gear includes layered clothing, a waterproof jacket, sturdy hiking boots, a sleeping bag rated for cold temperatures, trekking poles, a headlamp, and personal items like sunscreen, a hat, and a water bottle. Consult your tour operator for a comprehensive packing list.

faqs.title: How high is Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: Mount Kilimanjaro stands at approximately 5,895 meters (19,341 feet) above sea level, making it the highest peak in Africa.

faqs.title: What is altitude sickness, and how can I prevent it?
faqs.content: Altitude sickness occurs when your body struggles to acclimatize to high elevations, leading to symptoms like headache, nausea, and fatigue. To minimize the risk, ascend slowly, stay hydrated, and consider taking a medication like Diamox. Listen to your body and communicate with your guides.

faqs.title: Are there age restrictions for climbing Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: Yes, climbers must be at least 10 years old to trek Kilimanjaro, and those under 18 should be accompanied by an adult. Some operators have specific age limits, so check with your chosen tour company.

faqs.title: Will I need a guide to climb Mount Kilimanjaro?
faqs.content: Yes, all climbers are required to go with a licensed guide and a support team. This is essential for safety, navigation, and to comply with Tanzanian regulations.

faqs.title: What is the success rate for reaching the summit?
faqs.content: Success rates vary by route, but generally hover around 50-65% for shorter treks. Longer routes that allow for better acclimatization tend to have higher success rates, often exceeding 80%.

faqs.title: Is there a chance of communication during the climb?
faqs.content: You may have limited cell phone coverage on certain routes, but it’s advisable to expect minimal connectivity. Most trekkers focus on enjoying the experience and the beautiful surroundings rather than staying connected.

itinerary.title: Day 1
itinerary.content:
As you arrive at Kilimanjaro International Airport, our dedicated driver will be waiting for you, holding a sign with your name for a warm welcome. From there, you will enjoy a seamless and comfortable transfer to your Hotel.

Upon arrival, you’ll be served a delicious meal to replenish your energy. Later, our experienced mountain coordinators and your guide will provide a pre-trekking briefing, offering valuable insights into the wonders that await you on your expedition.

Take the time to relax in the inviting atmosphere of your Hotel, featuring a swimming pool, a beautiful garden, a bar, and a restaurant, ensuring a pleasant start to your adventure.

Overnight: Sal salinero hotel or similar

itinerary.title: Day 2
itinerary.desc: Moshi - Lemosho Park Gate - Mti Mkubwa Camp
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 2,200 m - 2,780 m
  • Hiking distance: 7 km
  • Hiking time: 5 hours

On your first day, after enjoying breakfast and attending a briefing with your guide at your

Hotel

, you’ll be transferred to

Lemosho Park Gate

(2,100m), a scenic 1.5-hour drive. At

Londorossi Gate

, you’ll complete the necessary registration before embarking on your trek.

The hike along picturesque forest trails to

Mti Mkubwa Campsite

(2,750m) typically takes around 3 hours. Upon your arrival, the porters will set up your tents, and our chef will prepare a hearty lunch for you to enjoy. After your meal, you’ll have some free time to relax and acclimatize before dinner.

In the evening, your guide will provide a detailed briefing about the next day’s trek, ensuring you are well-prepared for the adventure ahead.

itinerary.title: Day 3
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 2,780 m – 3,840 m
  • Hiking distance: 12 km
  • Hiking time: 6–7 hours

Begin your day with an early breakfast before setting out on your trek from

Mti Mkubwa Camp

. The trail will lead you through diverse landscapes, including lush moorlands and stunning views of

Kibo Volcano

. You’ll hike for approximately 5 hours, reaching

Shira Camp 1

, where a hot lunch prepared by our chef awaits you.

After your meal, continue the trek to

Shira Camp 2

, which is about 2-3 hours away. This campsite is located at a higher altitude, providing expansive views of the surrounding landscapes. Upon arrival, our porters will set up your tents, and you’ll have time to relax and acclimatize before dinner.

In the evening, your guide will provide a briefing on the following day’s trek, ensuring you are well-prepared for the adventure ahead.

itinerary.title: Day 4
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 3,840 m – 3,960 m
  • Hiking distance: 11 km
  • Hiking time: 7 to 8 hours

Start the day with an early wake-up call and a hearty breakfast to fuel your trek. Today’s route includes a climb to the

Lava Tower

at 4,630 meters, passing through a semi-desert, rocky landscape.

After approximately 5 hours of hiking, enjoy a well-deserved lunch before ascending the rocky scree path to the Lava Tower. This demanding day might test your endurance as you adjust to the higher altitude. After lunch, you’ll descend 680 meters to the

Barranco Camp

, where the true benefit of acclimatization becomes clear.

The 2-hour descent offers stunning photo opportunities of the

Western Breach

, a notable feature of Kilimanjaro’s landscape. End the day with a memorable sunset and a delicious dinner at Barranco Camp, where you can relax and reflect on the day’s adventures before preparing for the next leg of your journey.

itinerary.title: Day 5
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 3,960 m – 4,035 m
  • Hiking distance: 5 km
  • Hiking time: 5 hours

Start your day early with a wake-up call and a nourishing breakfast to fuel your trek. Today’s adventure involves ascending the famous

Barranco Wall

, a steep but rewarding section that offers stunning views of the surrounding landscapes. Once you conquer the Wall, you’ll descend into the picturesque

Karanga Valley

, known for its lush vegetation and breathtaking scenery. Upon reaching the

Karanga Camp

, our dedicated porters will set up the tents while our chef prepares a delicious lunch for you.

After your meal, you’ll embark on an acclimatization hike towards

Barafu Camp

, ascending 200 meters before returning to Karanga Camp. This hike is crucial for your body’s adjustment to the altitude.

In the evening, enjoy a hot meal prepared by our chef, and after dinner, your experienced guide will brief you on the next day’s trek, discussing the route, challenges, and essential details to ensure you’re well-prepared for the upcoming adventure.

itinerary.title: Day 6
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 4,035 m – 4,640 m
  • Hiking distance: 5 km
  • Hiking time: 5 hours

Start your day with an early wake-up call and a hearty breakfast to fuel your trek toward

Barafu Camp

. The trail features varied terrain, including rocky sections and gradual slopes, providing breathtaking views of Kilimanjaro’s high-altitude landscapes. As you ascend, it’s essential to focus on acclimatization to avoid altitude-related issues. Upon reaching

Barafu Camp

, our porters will efficiently handle the camp setup while the chef prepares a delicious lunch for you.

After enjoying your meal, take some time to rest and recharge until dinner. In the evening, your guide will brief you on the upcoming summit attempt, covering critical aspects such as the route, challenges, safety measures, and preparations to ensure you are ready for this significant part of your journey. Try to rest well tonight, as the summit ascent begins late in the evening, requiring your full energy and focus.

itinerary.title: Day 7
itinerary.desc: Summit Day | Barafu Camp | Uhuru Peak
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 4,640 m – 5, 895 m – 3,090 m
  • Hiking distance: 17 km
  • Hiking & descending time: 15+ hours

You’ll rise around

11:30 PM

and start your ascent after a light meal of tea and biscuits. Heading northwest, you’ll climb through scree towards

Stella Point

on the crater rim. This challenging

6-hour trek

to Stella Point (5,685m) is often the most mentally and physically demanding part of the climb.

After a brief rest at Stella Point, if weather conditions allow, you’ll be treated to a stunning sunrise. From Stella Point, it’s a

2-hour

snow-covered ascent to

Uhuru Peak

, the highest point on Kilimanjaro.

Your time at the summit will depend on the weather, so it’s important not to linger too long due to the cold and fatigue. The descent to

Barafu Camp

takes approximately

3 hours

, where you can take a short rest before continuing on to

Mweka Camp

for dinner and an overnight stay, reflecting on your incredible achievement.

itinerary.title: Day 8
itinerary.content:
• Altitude: 3,090 m – 1,650 m
  • Hiking distance: 10 km
  • Descending time: 4-5 hours

After breakfast at

Mweka Camp

, you’ll begin your descent to

Mweka Gate

, where your adventure concludes. A comfortable drive will take you back to

Moshi

, where a hot lunch and a refreshing shower await you, providing a well-deserved opportunity to relax.

At the end of your trip, tipping the team is encouraged and appreciated; special envelopes for this purpose will be available at the hotel. If you wish to extend your adventure with a safari, you can meet with our safari coordinator at the hotel. After some rest, the coordinator will provide a briefing on various safari options available.

We highly recommend booking a safari with us to experience Tanzania’s stunning wildlife and natural beauty, making your journey truly unforgettable.

Overnight: Sal salinero hotel or similar

itinerary.title: Day 9
itinerary.content:
After breakfast, you will be transferred back to Kilimanjaro International Airport for your departure. If you’re looking to extend your adventure, consider adding a day trip to your itinerary to explore nearby attractions or immerse yourself in the local culture. For more information, you can check our Day Trip page.

Alternatively, you might want to continue your journey with a visit to the stunning island of Zanzibar. Whether you seek relaxation on pristine beaches or wish to delve into the island’s rich culture, Zanzibar has something for everyone. Discover the perfect package for your next excursion by exploring our Zanzibar page.

If you’re also interested in adding a safari experience, please visit our Safari page for more details about our exciting safari options.
